A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from INSIGHT to CFM. Their core architecture, experiments, and appendix examples can be matched despite substantial rewriting and reformatting. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of both complete documents.

before.justification: V1 reports original concept-quality measurements, human-study outcomes, classification and segmentation experiments, and captioning results in Sections 4 and Appendices A–C.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds automated naming evaluation, dictionary and sparsity ablations, polysemanticity measurements, and revised downstream experiments.

M1.justification: The core CLIP-DINOiser and Matryoshka SAE architecture is retained, but downstream procedures change substantially. Appendix B.6 replaces GPT-2 with an eight-layer transformer adapter and ten prefix queries by Gemma-2-2B with a two-layer MLP projecting 196 spatial tokens. Section 4.2 and B.7 add AnyUp upsampling of concept activations before pixel-level reconstruction and segmentation.

E1.justification: Captioning training switches from COCO captions to CC12M DreamLIP long synthetic captions, substantially revising supervision for that task; CC12M was already used for SAE training. V2 also adds image-wise concept-presence evaluation on COCO in A.3. Classification and segmentation benchmark coverage and the human-study population remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds CLIP-DINOiser+AnyUp to the segmentation comparison and raw ViT neurons to the new polysemanticity comparison, and evaluates DN-CBM/MSAE in automated naming comparisons. CDM disappears from the swimming-hole qualitative panel but remains in the classification table. The earlier DN-CBM/MSAE locality comparisons are retained in Table C1, rather than removed.

E3.justification: Caption evaluation replaces BLEU-4, CIDEr, and METEOR with CLIPScore, RefCLIPScore, and CAPTURE, alongside a two-stage, 30,000-step Gemma/LoRA training setup. New protocols include top-ten concept-name judging with method-specific random controls, masked versus unmasked polysemanticity evaluation, and dictionary/sparsity sweeps. Appendix steering examples change from direct name lookup to Gemini-assisted concept selection.

E4.justification: New Tables B1–B3 test dictionary sizes and BatchTopK sparsity against downstream performance, interpretability, and reconstruction quality. Sections C.4–C.5 add polysemanticity and annotation-free consistency analyses, while C.3 and C.7 add naming-error examples and randomly sampled pixel-level segmentation cases. The explicit thresholded-versus-unthresholded segmentation comparison from v1 is no longer reported.

E5.justification: The five-annotator study design, participant filtering, SBERT distributions, and Wilcoxon rank-sum result remain unchanged; the naming significance result moves into the main text. Neither version reports experimental seed counts or confidence intervals. The new C2-Score boxplot describes variation across concept scores, not uncertainty across repeated runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds C2-Scores, automated naming outcomes, polysemanticity results, and ablation tables. Reported zero-shot classification changes from 59.6/38.7 to 68.6/41.2 on ImageNet/Places, and LF-CBM Places changes from 48.2 to 50.6; the proposed method remains at 78.9/55.4. Captioning results are replaced under different models and metrics. Segmentation scores are revised, with CFM and CFM+AnyUp averaging 41.3 and 41.9 mIoU; these changes do not establish performance gains under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The written hierarchy-confidence definition changes substantively: after matching parent/child indices, v1 Eq. (5) weights co-occurrence by the conditioned child's activation, whereas v2 Eq. (2) uses parent activation in the numerator and child activation in the denominator. This is not equivalent notation and does not guarantee the asserted [0,1] range. V2 also describes the graph as typically a DAG. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions—localized hierarchical concepts, relationship-aware naming, and interpretable downstream applications—remain. V2 broadens the framing from a foundation-like model supporting various tasks to the first concept-based foundation model providing explanations for any/all downstream vision tasks. This extends claim scope beyond a simple rename, while retaining the original research objective.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new polysemanticity results as reduced semantic entanglement and uses the ablations to justify dictionary size and sparsity choices. It qualifies annotation-free consistency performance as close to MSAE and adds a limitation concerning the applicability of existing explanation metrics to unsupervised concepts. Earlier naming limitations and illustrative failure cases remain in the appendices.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the automated judge prompt and concept-ranking controls, hierarchy-threshold selection guidance, and detailed AnyUp integration. Appendix B.6 documents the new captioning schedule, batch size, LoRA parameters, and approximately 22-hour training on one H100. Appendix A.4 newly specifies sliding-window segmentation, image resolutions, and background filtering; these disclosures alone do not establish changes from an explicitly stated v1 protocol.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations supporting VLM sparse autoencoders, LLaVA/Gemma-2, DreamLIP, AnyUp, polysemanticity evaluation, and captioning metrics. It removes v1's explicit attribution to Ye et al. as inspiration for feature-family discovery and emphasizes foundation-model positioning. The main related-work categories and most comparisons with prior approaches remain similar.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming INSIGHT to CFM, v2 substantially rewrites the introduction, contribution list, method exposition, and experimental narrative. Separate backbone and SAE subsections become a unified discussion of spatially localized representations, and downstream experiments are grouped under Foundation Model Applications. The appendices are reorganized and expanded with dedicated evaluation and analysis sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting and substantially reorganizes displays. V1's concept-quality table and human-study plot are combined in v2 Fig. 3; classification results and explanations are combined in Fig. 6. V2 adds naming comparisons, ablation tables, a C2-Score distribution plot, and pixel-level examples, and redraws captioning and concept-vector illustrations. Many existing appendix examples are retained with new placement.

improvement.justification: The new dictionary/sparsity ablations and independent concept-quality checks address validation gaps in v1, while the judge prompt and detailed caption-training recipe improve reproducibility. These support a modest net quality gain. Benefits are tempered by claims covering all downstream tasks despite limited demonstrated coverage, and by the revised hierarchy-confidence formula, which no longer guarantees its stated probability range. The changed captioning and segmentation results also do not establish improvements under unchanged conditions.
